title: How do you answer "How would you find that out?" in a case interview?
description: "How would you find that out?" for case interviews. When the interviewer asks how you would get data. A checklist, a worked example and how to say it.
hook: Sometimes the most useful thing you can say in a case is how you would find something out. Here is a list of sources and methods you can point to.
body:
When it helps

When the interviewer asks how you would get data.

The checklist

Ask customers

  • Surveys
  • Focus groups
  • Pilots and A/B tests

Ask experts

  • Internal specialists
  • Industry experts

Use data

  • Industry reports
  • Historical trends
  • The client's own data

An example

The interviewer asks how you would know whether customers would pay more for faster delivery. You could survey existing customers, run a small pilot in one city with two different prices (an A/B test), talk to the delivery team about what customers ask for, and look at what rivals charge for express delivery. Mentioning a quick, cheap test is usually the strongest answer.

How it sounds in an interview

I'd find out in three ways: ask customers through a short survey, test it with a small pilot, and check what the data and rivals already tell us.

Match the method to the uncertainty

A supermarket says shoppers have stopped buying its premium ready meals. First define what needs explaining: fewer shoppers entering the category, lower conversion among shoppers who see the products, lower purchase frequency, or a move to competitors. Then choose evidence for each.

Transaction data can show when sales changed, where it happened and whether prices or promotions shifted. In-store observations can reveal poor shelf placement or empty shelves. Short customer interviews can reveal perceptions about quality or price. Competitor checks can identify launches or discounts at the same time. None of those methods alone proves causality.

A useful test is to compare matched stores where the product remained in stock against those with stockouts. If the decline is concentrated in the latter, availability becomes the leading hypothesis. Explain what result would confirm or reject each hypothesis before requesting another dataset. That is what makes research a decision tool rather than a long list of things to investigate.
